overview: This 355-page file documents Japanese trade unions and U.S. occupation labor policy from 1946 to 1949. It combines a history of teachers’ unions, nationwide membership and activity statistics, petitions, legal analyses, and diplomatic correspondence. Major subjects include public employees’ labor rights, Toshiba’s proposed deconcentration, union officials’ political screening, and Japanese participation in international labor organizations.
interest: The file links detailed union statistics and firsthand petitions to occupation decisions, showing how labor rights were contested.
